mechanism: Scopolamine's anticholinergic effects may oppose atenolol's beta-blocking properties and increase heart rate, while both drugs can cause CNS depression and anticholinergic effects may reduce gastric motility affecting atenolol absorption.
action: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure closely; consider alternative anticholinergic agent or adjust atenolol dose if scopolamine use is necessary; counsel patient on additive CNS depression risk.
